Nyzhne Solotvyno Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyzhnie Solotvyno, Ukraine

Not demolished. This cemetery existed by 1867 per its oldest tombstone, with its newest surviving stone dated 1931, presumably in use until WWII. Jews are believed to have arrived in the late 18th century; population reached 11 by 1851, growing to 73 by 1880, then declining to 60 by 1900 and 57 by 1921. Jews worked in agriculture and commerce; population fell to 32 by 1930. Hungarian forces arrived in March 1939, drafting some Jews into forced labor battalions by 1941, with others sent to the Eastern Front where most perished. Population reached 45 by 1941; families without Hungarian citizenship were expelled that year to Kamianets-Podilskyi in Nazi-occupied Ukraine and murdered. Remaining Jews were deported to Auschwitz in late May 1944. No Jews live in the town today.
